figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Biophysical and biochemical characterization of PptT. (A) Schematic representation of the post-translational phosphopantetheinylation
by a PPTase. The PPTase transfers the PPant moiety from CoA to a conserved serine residue on the apo-ACP, resulting in the formation of the
holo-ACP. (B) Thermal stability of PptT purified in the absence of divalent cations and following subsequent addition of 1 mM M2+(Ca2+, Mg2+,
Mn2+, Co2+, and Ni2+) and 50 μM CoA or 3′,5′-ADP. The empty histogram bars represent approximate Tm values. (C) Activation time-course of
the ACP domain (2042−2188) of PpsC by PptT. The transfer of the Ppant group from CoA to the ACP domain is visualized on a 10% native
polyacrylamide gel supplemented with 2.5 M urea, either in the absence of M2+ or in the presence of 1 mM CaCl2, MgCl2, or MnCl2 at 15 and 60
min intervals. The control corresponds to the inactivated form of the ACP domain.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Crystal structures of PptT. Ribbon representations of PptT are shown for the (A) apo form and for the complexes with (B) CoA and (C)
3′,5′-ADP. Electron density 2Fo-Fc SA omit maps are contoured at the 1s level. (D) To highlight differences in the positioning of key residues and
cations, a structural superimposition of all three structures is presented. Residue side chains and CoA are depicted in ball-and-stick mode and color-
coded according to atom type (blue for nitrogen, red for oxygen, black for phosphate, and orange for sulfur). The Mn2+ and Mg2+ ions at sites I and
II are colored dark purple and light purple, respectively. Water molecules are represented as red spheres. All figures are in the same orientation.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Crystal structure of the PptT-CoA/ACP complex. (A) The surface representation depicts four PPTases (colored in blue, yellow, purple,
and green) and two ACPs (shaded in light and dark gray) within the asymmetric unit. CoA molecules are visualized in a ball-and-stick
representation following the color code introduced in Figure 2. (B,C) Close-up views showing the ACP domain sandwiched between two PptT
molecules. Patches of residues involved in polar and nonpolar interactions at the PptT-ACP interface identified using the PDBePISA server44 are
colored brown. Hydrogen bond interactions are depicted as black dashed lines. The position of mutated S2105A is indicated with a brown sphere.
Figures in (B,C) are presented in the same orientation.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Tunnel entrance for the pantothenic acid group of CoA. Surface representation of residues E157, Y160, W170, and F173 delineating the
tunnel entrance of PptT (A) in the absence and (B) in the presence of CoA. Interactions with the Ppant arm are predominantly of van der Waals
nature. Distance values between the closest carbon atoms are indicated. CoA and residues are shown as sticks (carbon and phosphate, black;
nitrogen, blue; and oxygen, red).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. View of the CoA ligand in PptT alone and in complex with the ACP domain, obtained through MD simulations. In the absence of ACP,
the main conformations of CoA are shown, with Oβ-Pβ-Oα-Pα dihedral angle values of (A) 176 and (B) −77°. In the Pβ-Oα-Pα bridge, the Oα
oxygen atom is alternatively oriented inside and outside the active site. In both cases, the interaction between the Mg2+ ion and the Oβ atom is not
affected and remains stable at around 1.9 Å. (C) In the presence of ACP, the Oβ-Pβ-Oα-Pα dihedral angle is stabilized around a value of 160°,
similar to the one observed in (A). However, the Pβ phosphate group has been rotated and is replaced by a water molecule that coordinates with
the Mg2+ ion. The ACP residue S2105 establishes stable hydrogen bonds with the residue E157 and the β-phosphate group. All figures are
presented in the same orientation.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Schematic representations of the simulated reaction mechanism. (A) Starting from the top, a schematic representation and a reduced
view of the reactant’s active site, labeled R, are provided. On the left side, we illustrate the proton transfer concerted to nucleophilic attack, modeled
by step 1a, which leads to the formation of IM1a. Following this, in step 2a, we showcase the dissociation of the 3′,5′-ADP moiety from the PptT-
CoA/ACP complex, leading to the formation of IM2a. Finally, step 3 follows step 2a, during which the 3′,5′-ADP moiety abstracts a proton from an
activated metal-bound water molecule, leading to P1a. On the right side, we present the alternative step 1b pathway, where the proton is abstracted
by an activated metal-bound water molecule, leading to the formation of IM1b. Finally, we illustrate the step 2b pathway, where the dissociation of
the 3′,5′-ADP is catalyzed by the protonation of Oα, resulting in the formation of P1b. (B) Energy profile for the phosphopantetheinyl transfer
reaction. The energy profile was obtained from the CI extrapolation of external works performed through SMD. Black dashed lines indicate the
energy profile of step 1a, while blue dashed lines represent its alternative pathway, step 1b. The energy profile corresponding to step 2a is depicted
in green dashed lines, while steps 2b and 3 are indicated by red and dark-red dashed lines, respectively. Snapshots of the active sites are represented
in the same orientation.
